airport: broad paved aviation area with runway-like surfaces and sparse surrounding airport infrastructure, distinguishing airport from railwaystation by lacking concentrated rail lines and station-node organization.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary, distinguishing beach from pond by broader coastal extent and from river by lacking a narrow winding channel.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from viaduct by a more localized crossing form, from river by being a crossing rather than a continuous watercourse, and from commercial by lacking dense building-block organization.
commercial: organized urban built-up area with dense man-made structures and road access, distinguishing commercial from parking by stronger building dominance, from bridge by lacking a narrow crossing form, and from park by weaker vegetation presence and stronger built-up structure.
desert: dry barren land with sparse vegetation and homogeneous exposed-ground texture, visually distinct from other classes by its broad arid surface and lack of strong water, vegetation, or built structure.
farmland: regular cultivated land with visible plot boundaries and agricultural texture, distinguishing farmland from meadow by stronger man-made parcel organization.
footballfield: rectangular sports field with clear field-like geometry and managed grass surface, distinguishing footballfield from meadow by stronger sports-ground structure.
forest: dense natural tree canopy with dark-green continuous vegetation texture, distinguishing forest from mountain by weaker terrain relief and more canopy-dominant appearance.
industrial: factory-like compounds with utilitarian structures, storage areas, and production-oriented layout, distinguishing industrial from parking by stronger building-yard structure, from railwaystation by weaker rail-line concentration, and from port by lacking strong dock-water context.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture, distinguishing meadow from footballfield by lacking formal sports-field geometry and from farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with clear relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from forest by stronger terrain variation.
park: planned green open space with vegetation and leisure-oriented layout, distinguishing park from pond by being land-dominant rather than water-dominant and from commercial by stronger vegetation presence and weaker building density.
parking: open paved area with vehicle-oriented organization and parking-row structure, distinguishing parking from commercial by weaker building dominance, from industrial by weaker factory-compound structure, and from viaduct by lacking elevated crossing form.
pond: small enclosed water body with compact shape and visible boundary, distinguishing pond from park by being water-dominant, from river by lacking a long winding channel, and from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline.
port: waterfront transport area with dock-side infrastructure and shore-adjacent logistics organization, distinguishing port from industrial by stronger harbor-water context, from river by wider dock-organized shoreline structure, and from commercial by clearer waterfront transport layout.
railwaystation: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railwaystation from industrial by clearer rail-line concentration, from airport by lacking broad aviation pavement and runway context, and from viaduct by stronger station-node organization.
residential: built-up neighborhood with repeated housing roofs and regular living-area layout, distinguishing residential from industrial by weaker factory-yard structure and from commercial by smaller more repetitive housing roofs.
river: elongated natural watercourse with a continuous winding channel, distinguishing river from pond by stronger linear flow shape, from bridge by being water rather than a crossing structure, and from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline.
viaduct: elongated elevated transport structure with clear grade-separated linear form, distinguishing viaduct from bridge by a more extended raised-traffic pattern, from parking by lacking flat vehicle rows, and from railwaystation by lacking concentrated station-like rail organization.
